premises.text: People default to familiar places because they will not risk new venues without confidence they will like the experience
premises.evidence_span: we don't want to take the chance and try to go to a new place because we're not sure that we're going to like the experience

premises.text: SpotOn personalizes actionable place recommendations from Facebook/Foursquare social data and user ratings/check-ins
premises.evidence_span: pulling in your existing social network data from Facebook and Foursquare, uses it to build a profile of you to give you personalized and actionable recommendations

premises.text: A social layer shows friends' ratings, visits, bookmarks, and who to go with—not anonymous reviewers
premises.evidence_span: Every single place has a social layer that pulls in reasons why you should go check out a place

premises.text: In-app fun rating/contribution of preference data improves recommendations for the user and builds a shared new information layer for everyone
premises.evidence_span: we make it really easy for our users to give us a lot of their preference data in a really fun and an engaging way

premises.text: Filters and search surface personalized top recommendations, bookmarks, friends' loves, and new-vs-visited place views
premises.evidence_span: with one touch of a button, I can say, only show me places that at least one of my friends have been to

premises.text: Pipeline group recommendations and in-app planning turn discovery into shared physical-world experiences
premises.evidence_span: SpotOn is not about the recommendation. It is about the end experience of being at that bar with your friends

value.text: Easiest way to go to new places with friends and enjoy the end experience together
value.evidence_span: the easiest way to go to new places with your friends

causal_links.evidence_span: we don't want to take the chance and try to go to a new place
changing the way that friends come together in the physical world

notes: Map/pix/detail UI cascade folded into personalization+social product (§4.1.7). Friend ratings and who-to-go-with are facets of the social layer. Filters/search kept with product as presentation cascade. Group planning kept as separately framed experience module (P6). Singleton D1: risk-aversion problem independently revisable.
